front_blocks.md: Why is carbon essential to living organisms?

back_blocks.md: It is an essential part of the **biological molecules** from which cells are built — **carbohydrates, proteins and fats**.

cards.front_md: Why is carbon essential to living organisms?
cards.back_md: It is an essential part of the **biological molecules** from which cells are built — **carbohydrates, proteins and fats**.

front_blocks.md: How is carbon taken out of the atmosphere?

back_blocks.md: By plants during **photosynthesis**, which takes in **carbon dioxide** and uses the carbon to make **glucose**.

cards.front_md: How is carbon taken out of the atmosphere?
cards.back_md: By plants during **photosynthesis**, which takes in **carbon dioxide** and uses the carbon to make **glucose**.

front_blocks.md: What happens to the carbon a plant takes in?

back_blocks.md: It is used to make **glucose**, which can be turned into **carbohydrates, fats and proteins** within the plant's **biomass**.

cards.front_md: What happens to the carbon a plant takes in?
cards.back_md: It is used to make **glucose**, which can be turned into **carbohydrates, fats and proteins** within the plant's **biomass**.

front_blocks.md: How is carbon transferred between living organisms?

back_blocks.md: By **feeding** — from plants to animals when herbivores feed, and between animals when carnivores feed.

cards.front_md: How is carbon transferred between living organisms?
cards.back_md: By **feeding** — from plants to animals when herbivores feed, and between animals when carnivores feed.

front_blocks.md: How does respiration return carbon to the atmosphere?

back_blocks.md: **Respiration** in plants and animals releases carbon as **carbon dioxide**.

cards.front_md: How does respiration return carbon to the atmosphere?
cards.back_md: **Respiration** in plants and animals releases carbon as **carbon dioxide**.

front_blocks.md: How does decomposition return carbon to the atmosphere?

back_blocks.md: **Microorganisms** such as bacteria and fungi use **dead and waste material** to fuel their respiration, releasing carbon dioxide.

cards.front_md: How does decomposition return carbon to the atmosphere?
cards.back_md: **Microorganisms** such as bacteria and fungi use **dead and waste material** to fuel their respiration, releasing carbon dioxide.

back_blocks.md: When animals and plants **die in conditions where decomposers are not present**, the carbon in their bodies is converted into **fossil fuels**.

cards.back_md: When animals and plants **die in conditions where decomposers are not present**, the carbon in their bodies is converted into **fossil fuels**.

front_blocks.md: How does combustion return carbon to the atmosphere?

back_blocks.md: **Burning fossil fuels** releases the carbon stored in them as **carbon dioxide**.

front_blocks.md: Only animals return carbon dioxide to the atmosphere by respiration.

back_blocks.md: Respiration occurs in **plants as well as animals**, and in the **microorganisms** that decompose dead material.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Only animals return carbon dioxide to the atmosphere by respiration.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Respiration occurs in **plants as well as animals**, and in the **microorganisms** that decompose dead material.

front_blocks.md: Fossil fuels form when dead matter is decomposed by bacteria.

back_blocks.md: Fossil fuels form when organisms die **where decomposers are not present**, so the carbon is not released.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Fossil fuels form when dead matter is decomposed by bacteria.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Fossil fuels form when organisms die **where decomposers are not present**, so the carbon is not released.
